subject.title: Support Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk via gateway relay

question: Which Azure Realtime credential and endpoint contract should OpenClaw support first for Gateway Relay Talk?
rationale: The remaining implementation decides whether API-key auth, Microsoft Entra ID, redirect handling, config shape, and browser fallback behavior keep Azure credentials server-side without creating unsafe provider-routing behavior.

options.title: API-Key Relay First, Entra Follow-Up
options.body: Implement the constrained Gateway Relay path for Azure API keys with SecretRef/Key Vault guidance, Azure-specific errors, no browser credential exposure, and leave Microsoft Entra ID as a documented follow-up.

options.title: Require Entra Before First-Class Support
options.body: Hold implementation until Microsoft Entra ID or managed identity is designed alongside API-key support, reducing long-term credential risk at the cost of delaying Azure Talk users.

options.title: Close As External Plugin Work
options.body: Move Azure Realtime Talk outside core only if maintainers decide the bundled OpenAI provider should not own Azure deployment support despite the existing provider fields.

recommendation.title: API-Key Relay First, Entra Follow-Up
recommendation.body: Implement the constrained Gateway Relay path for Azure API keys with SecretRef/Key Vault guidance, Azure-specific errors, no browser credential exposure, and leave Microsoft Entra ID as a documented follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the GA realtime bridge and recent OpenAI realtime auth work in the same provider path.
